intent.outcome: Mutations to milestone state keep the plan.toml index authoritative and consistent with the per-milestone files with no manual step, any value drift is detectable by mp validate, and mp sync is documented as the recovery path.

problem.description: Field testing (lazybrew adoption, I-09, on mp 1.4.0) found that after `mp milestone approve`, per-milestone files flip spec_status to 'ready' but the plan.toml index kept the prior value, and `mp validate` passed despite the drift. mp 1.5.0 already ships a top-level `mp sync` that rebuilds the index (confirmed during this planning session: it re-added M31-M35 and silently updated stale M19/M21 entries), but three gaps remain: (1) mutations (create/approve/set-spec-status/set-status/complete) do NOT auto-sync, so drift accumulates until someone manually runs `mp sync`; (2) `mp validate` only warns on *missing* entries (W01) and does not detect *stale-value* drift - the M19/M21 silent updates prove value drift goes undetected; (3) `mp sync` is undocumented in MP-COMMANDS.md. Index drift is a recurring pain (M16's own spec also complains about a stale plan.toml index).

in_scope: Auto-sync the plan.toml index on every state mutation (create/approve/set-spec-status/set-status/complete) so a manual `mp sync` is not required
`mp validate` detects stale-value drift (index spec_status/execution_status/title disagreeing with the milestone file), distinct from the existing W01 missing-entry warning
Document the existing `mp sync` command in MP-COMMANDS.md (and AGENT-PLAYBOOK as the recovery path)
Integration tests: mutation auto-syncs; validate detects induced stale-value drift; mp sync rebuilds
out_of_scope: A new `mp plan sync` command (the top-level `mp sync` already exists)
Removing the plan.toml index entirely (keep it as a snapshot, kept correct)
